major.name: Translation Studies - Minor

requirement.text: Level 1-6 of a language other than English (or equivalent)
requirement.label: Language Requirement

items.label: B. Language Specific Workshop:
items.description: One UD course taught in the chosen language of study
items.notes: Also includes: CHIN 106A. For courses in Classics (Greek and Latin), German, Japanese, Portuguese, Religious Studies (Hebrew, Pashto, Persian, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tibetan, Turkish, Urdu, etc.), and Russian, consult the Translation Studies Faculty Advisor and the Faculty Advisor from the language section of your desired focus. Approval by the TS Faculty Advisor is required.

items.label: C. Two UD Electives
items.description: (Subject to approval by the Comparative Literature Department or from the list provided)
items.notes: *Note that students who are pursuing a major or a minor in Comparative Literature may not select elective Comparative Literature courses that are applicable to the major or minor.

items.label: Upper-Division Requirements
items.description: 20 UD units are required, distributed as follows:

items.label: D.
items.notes: Translation studies capstone project with the faculty advisor from the language department of the student’s focus. Areas A and B must be completed before moving on to Area D.

narrative: All courses to be applied to the minor must be completed on a letter-grade basis. This includes both courses offered in comparative literature and those offered by other departments and applied to the minor.

Substitutions and waivers are subject to approval by the chair of the department.
Students must consult the General Catalog for prerequisites to required courses.
The following conditions must also be met for official recognition of the minor:
- The sponsoring department reports completion of the minor prior to the posting of the degree.
- At least 18 upper-division quarter units are completed for the minor. (Waivers cannot reduce the requirement below this number.)
- The UC grade-point average in ALL applied upper-division courses is 2.0 or higher.
- No more than 5 upper-division units overlap between this minor and the upper-division portion of themajor(s) or other minor(s). If overlap is greater with the major(s), completion of the minor will not be formally recognized; if overlap with other minor(s) is greater, only the first minor reported will be recognized

nodes.title: Introduction to Translation I
nodes.description: Comprises topics necessary to develop skills that are needed for writing at a specialized level and to carry out written translation into and from Spanish, mostly texts on business and medical topics.

nodes.title: China in Translation: Theory, Art, History
nodes.description: Uses case studies of translations into and out of China--long regarded as a civilization distinct from the West--to explore themes in translation studies. Topics include ideograms, orientalism, modernization, world literature, annotation, musicality, poetic license, and adaptation.

nodes.title: Translation as Metaphor: Introduction to Translation Theory and Practice
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; and completion of quarter 5 or equivalent of the language of study.

items.text: completion of quarter 5 or equivalent of the language of study

nodes.description: The course aims to develop skills in terminology and technologies of translation; it also examines the practical and theoretical issues pertaining to translation as an artistic, cultural, and ethical process. Focus on literary translation as creative research and practice.

nodes.title: Research in Translation Studies
nodes.description: Individualized instruction to complete the capstone translation project for the Minor in Translation Studies. To be completed with the faculty advisor from the language department of the student's focus.

nodes.title: China in Translation: Theory, Art, History
nodes.description: Uses case studies of translations into and out of China--long regarded as a civilization distinct from the West--to explore themes in translation studies. Topics include ideograms, orientalism, modernization, world literature, annotation, musicality, poetic license, and adaptation.

nodes.title: Intermediate French
nodes.description: First in the three-quarter intermediate French series. Builds on foundation established in first-year and includes thorough review of French grammar. Speaking and writing skills developed through exposure to French and Francophone culture, literature, and film. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French
nodes.description: A continuation of French 4. Discussion encouraged through oral reports on such topics as Impressionist art and French film. Readings include poetry, plays, and short stories. Web-based activities add to the interest of the course. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French
nodes.description: Continuation of French 5. Students complete their grammar review. Continued emphasis on speaking and writing through an examination of contemporary French culture, with exposure to some of the important trends in French intellectual history, notably Existentialism. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French for Global Studies and Political Science
nodes.description: Students complete review of French grammar. Continued emphasis on speaking, reading, and writing through study of French and Francophone history, politics, language policy, and culture within a global and larger European context. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Critical Writing in French
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: This advanced composition course focuses on enhancing students’ analytical skills through an examination of French argumentative modes and critical reading of texts (literature, journalistic essays, political and philosophical works). The goal for students is to develop a clear, persuasive argument on specific works and major issues both orally and in writing. Course includes a comprehensive analysis of complex grammatical structures and the enhancement of French vocabulary for a range of communicative contexts.

nodes.title: Writing the Self
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Readings in twentieth-century autobiography serving as models for creative writing. Coursework involves analysis of literary works and a long-term ‘autobiographical project’ that may be factual or fictionalized. Course includes a practice of complex grammatical structures and the enhancement of French vocabulary.

nodes.title: Advanced French Grammar
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Course is designed to provide a thorough review of the rules of French grammar and to situate the discussions within linguistic and cultural contexts, covering topics such as semantics, syntax, and inclusive writing. Explores linguistic features and political contexts of domestic and global varieties of the language. Additional foci include continued vocabulary enrichment, increased syntactic accuracy, and composition skills in French.

nodes.title: Business Communication and Cultural Affairs
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Study of specific vocabulary, formulae, and writing strategies useful for individual career objectives in the business world. Students will acquire a foundation in contemporary business and professional French, developed through the analysis and application of business concepts and the composition of analytic essays and business documents.

nodes.title: Finance and Marketing in French
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Students study essential aspects of the conduct of business in France, as well as specific features of the French language, both spoken and written, commonly encountered in business practice. Prepares students to take the (optional) competency exam for the Diplôme de français professionnel B2, which is offered annually by the Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie de Paris (CCIP). The continuation of Business French 1, but not limited to students who have taken that course.

nodes.title: Literary Translation: Theory and Practice
nodes.prereq_text: 1 course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Exploration of the various theories of translation. Offers a practical component where students work on a specific translation project. Examination of literary, philosophical, linguistic and theoretical texts by Jakobson, Benjamin, Steiner, Derrida and others.

nodes.title: Elementary Italian
nodes.description: Introduction to the most basic elements of Italian grammar. Articles, adjectives, gender. Verbs in the present tense.

nodes.title: Elementary Italian
nodes.description: Logical continuation of Italian 1. Direct and indirect pronouns. Verbs in the past tense and the imperfect. Emphasis on the correct writing and speaking of Italian.

nodes.title: Elementary Italian
nodes.description: Continuation of Italian 2. Verbs in the future, conditional. Introduction to subjunctive. Further emphasis on the correct writing and speaking of Italian.

nodes.title: Intermediate Italian
nodes.description: Intended to develop the linguistic skills of students who have completed the first year. Review of basic grammar structures with emphasis on exceptions, enrichment of vocabulary, reading comprehension, and discussion of modern short stories. In Italian.

nodes.title: Intermediate Italian
nodes.description: Increases the students' reading, writing, and speaking skills. Review of more complex grammar structures through written exercises, enrichment of vocabulary, reading comprehension and discussion of contemporary short stories. In Italian.

nodes.title: Intermediate Italian
nodes.description: Further develops the students' reading, writing, and speaking skills. Intensive review of the most advanced grammar structures: subjunctive, passive voice, indirect discourse. Reading and discussion of contemporary short stories. In Italian.

nodes.title: The Art of Translation
nodes.description: (Taught in Italian) An intensive workshop exploring the theory and practice of translation. Students work at translating literary texts from Italian to English and vice versa.

nodes.title: Italian Culture in Translation
nodes.description: (Taught in Italian) Focuses on forms of cultural translation between Italy and America. Examples of these translations: American travelers in Italy to nineteenth-century translators of Dante, from emigrant culture to the mafia to the 'spaghetti' western to Italian hip-hop.

nodes.title: Elementary Arabic I
nodes.description: Introductory modern standard Arabic: pronunciation, script, conversation, and oral comprehension. Weekly sections involve cultural materials such as elementary calligraphy, Middle Eastern cooking, Arabic television shows, films, singing, and folk dance.

nodes.title: Elementary Arabic II
nodes.description: Continuation of Arabic I.

nodes.title: Elementary Arabic III
nodes.description: Continuation of Arabic II.

nodes.title: Intermediate Arabic IV
nodes.description: Intermediate Arabic: complex grammar, and vocabulary, readings in classical and modern Arabic literature, including short stories, newspaper articles, and poetry. Extensive use of audio-visual materials including news broadcasts, television shows, and films. weekly conversation section.

nodes.title: Intermediate Arabic V
nodes.description: Continuation of Arabic IV.

nodes.title: Intermediate Arabic VI
nodes.description: Continuation of Arabic V.

nodes.title: Advanced Arabic
nodes.description: Advanced study of grammar and vocabulary; readings in the major genres of classical and modern Arabic literature, including Qur'an, medieval poetry and prose, modern short story and novels, etc.

nodes.title: Advanced Arabic
nodes.description: Continuation of Relgious Studies 148A.

nodes.title: Advanced Arabic
nodes.description: Continuation of Relgious Studies 148B.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice and Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-mid level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: SPAN 1HY is the first course in a three-part hybrid Spanish series (SPAN 1HY, 2HY, 3HY), equivalent to the SPAN 1, 2, 3 Elementary Spanish sequence. Combining face-to-face instruction with online work, this course uses a communicative approach to develop basic Spanish skills for real-life situations. Class time focuses on active communication, with 99% of instruction conducted in Spanish. Students will build foundational grammar skills and gain insight into the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. By the end of the course, students are expected to reach Novice-Mid proficiency.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 or Spanish W1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice and Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 or Spanish 1HY with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN 2HY is the second of the three Hybrid Elementary Spanish courses. Its hybrid format combines increased individual work with the online textbook, materials, and other web-based activities with reduced face-to-face class time and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in SPAN 2. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 2 or Spanish W2 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice; Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high or Intermediate-low level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Completion of Spanish 2 or Spanish 2HY with a grade of P, or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN 3HY is the third of the three Hybrid Elementary Spanish courses. Its hybrid format combines increased individual work with the online textbook, materials, and other web-based activities with reduced face-to-face class time and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in SPAN 3. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish I
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 3, Spanish 3SS, 3HY, with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Language & Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Begins review of basic grammar and syntax.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 4 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Language and Culture Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Continues the review of basic grammar and syntax. Course conducted in Spanish.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 5 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Language and Culture Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Literature Examination; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: An intensive course designed to develop students' skills in reading, oral, and written expression by reading and discussing Hispanic texts, and writing compositions on related topics.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.prereq_text: Instructor or department approval required to finalize enrollment.
nodes.description: SPAN 15 is designed for students who learned Spanish at home or as a first language and provides them with the language and learning skills required to successfully complete more advanced Spanish courses (SPAN 16A/B). It focuses on formal Spanish, grammar, and reading with an emphasis on writing and vocabulary building. Students will develop awareness of linguistic registers, and practice formal speaking and writing skills through readings and discussions based on Hispanic topics in the United States and other Spanish-speaking countries. Special attention will be paid to those aspects that Spanish speakers in the United States find most problematic.

nodes.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.description: Addresses on a university level the needs and strengths of students with Spanish speaking background but no formal language training in Spanish speaking countries. Emphasizes skill in composition, advanced reading comprehension, standard versus vernacular usages, cross language interference, etc.

nodes.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 16A with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Addresses on university level the needs and strengths of students with Spanish speaking background but no formal language training in Spanish speaking countries. Emphasizes more complex skills in composition and advanced reading comprehension than Spanish 16A, as well as standard versus vernacular usages, cross language interferences, etc.

nodes.title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 6 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 4 or 5 on the AP Spanish Literature Examination; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Intensive course taught in Spanish designed to reinforce students' comprehension and ability to express themselves in Spanish, both orally and in writing, and to develop the students' vocabularies and awareness of syntactical structures in the language.

nodes.title: Introduction to Translation I
nodes.description: Comprises topics necessary to develop skills that are needed for writing at a specialized level and to carry out written translation into and from Spanish, mostly texts on business and medical topics.

nodes.title: Online Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: Span W1 is the first course of the Elementary Spanish three course sequence delivered in a fully online format. By the end of this course students are expected to develop basic proficiency in Spanish at the Novice-mid level.

nodes.title: Online Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN W 2 is the second of the three Elementary Spanish courses offered in a fully online format. Its online format combines technology-based language instruction with online class meetings and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in the regular Elementary Span II course. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. Each week, students attend one online class session and one conversation session. There is individual work with the textbook, online materials, and other web-based activities.
